answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared lagoon escrow before trading. The stake is released only after verified useful work, so hollow identities that never deliver forfeit it. A velvet reputation layer then caps how much new, unproven identities may move per day. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes must fund every stake and wait out the cap, so cost grows linearly with each fake while honest agents pay nothing beyond the refundable deposit.
